chapter: Chapter 1: The Miseries of the Sinful in this World and the Other
chapter_title: The Miseries of the Sinful in this World and the Other
text: Garuda, son of Vinata, with devotion spoke unto the Blessed Lord Vishnu: Tell me, O Lord, what is the path of beings in this world, and what becomes of those who turn away from righteousness, and how the fruits of actions follow every soul.

chapter: Chapter 1: The Miseries of the Sinful in this World and the Other
chapter_title: The Miseries of the Sinful in this World and the Other
text: The Blessed Lord said: Hear, O Garuda, the truth regarding the fruits of action. A man gathers the fruit of his own deeds, whether good or evil. No one else bestows sorrow or joy upon him; his own accumulated acts become his companion and shape his destiny.

chapter: Chapter 1: The Miseries of the Sinful in this World and the Other
chapter_title: The Miseries of the Sinful in this World and the Other
text: Whatever deed is performed by mind, speech, or body leaves its impression upon the inner being. He who sows discord through harsh speech reaps distress, while he who speaks truthfully and gently creates tranquility for himself and others.

chapter: Chapter 1: The Miseries of the Sinful in this World and the Other
chapter_title: The Miseries of the Sinful in this World and the Other
text: Wealth, youth, and life are fleeting like bubbles upon water. He who forgets righteousness in the pursuit of selfish gain is like a traveler who falls asleep upon a perilous path when the storm approaches.

chapter: Chapter 2: The Way of Yama and the Reckoning
chapter_title: The Way of Yama and the Reckoning
text: In the realm of justice, there is no falsehood and no favoritism. Deeds alone stand witness for the traveler. Neither kinship, nor pride of lineage, nor accumulated treasure avails anything where only virtue and truth are weighed.

chapter: Chapter 2: The Way of Yama and the Reckoning
chapter_title: The Way of Yama and the Reckoning
text: He who in life gave water to the thirsty and shelter to the weary finds the road cool and shadowed. The small kindnesses shown to the helpless become shields upon the journey of the soul.

chapter: Chapter 2: The Way of Yama and the Reckoning
chapter_title: The Way of Yama and the Reckoning
text: The soul that has practiced harmlessness towards living beings and shared its bread with the hungry walks without fear, attended by the fragrance of its own good deeds.

chapter: Chapter 3: The Fruits of Cruelty and Neglect
chapter_title: The Fruits of Cruelty and Neglect
text: Those who oppress the weak, who mock the afflicted, or who break trust with those who confided in them experience the bitterness of their own hardness of heart. Cruelty burns the one who harbors it even before it reaches the victim.

chapter: Chapter 3: The Fruits of Cruelty and Neglect
chapter_title: The Fruits of Cruelty and Neglect
text: A promise made to a friend or dependent must be honored as sacred. He who betrays a friend or turns his back on one who sought refuge incurs deep sorrow and loses the clarity of his intellect.

chapter: Chapter 4: The Kinds of Transgressions and Moral Duties
chapter_title: The Kinds of Transgressions and Moral Duties
text: He who disrespects his mother and father, who neglects them in their old age after having been nurtured by their devotion, forgets the root of his own existence and wanders in darkness.

chapter: Chapter 4: The Kinds of Transgressions and Moral Duties
chapter_title: The Kinds of Transgressions and Moral Duties
text: Bearing false witness, concealing the truth to gain unlawful profit, and slandering the innocent poison both the family and the self. Truthfulness alone upholds the universe and preserves society from decay.

chapter: Chapter 4: The Kinds of Transgressions and Moral Duties
chapter_title: The Kinds of Transgressions and Moral Duties
text: Taking that which has not been given, whether by open force or subtle stealth, binds the thief to anxiety and suspicion. Contentment with one's rightful earnings is the supreme medicine against greed.

chapter: Chapter 4: The Kinds of Transgressions and Moral Duties
chapter_title: The Kinds of Transgressions and Moral Duties
text: Anger is the slayer of wisdom; it destroys the merit of good deeds and blinds the eye of discernment. He who conquers anger before it conquers him is recognized as a true hero among men.

chapter: Chapter 8: The Power of Charity (Dana) and Selfless Giving
chapter_title: The Power of Charity (Dana) and Selfless Giving
text: Gifts given with a pure heart to those in genuine need produce fruit without end. Charity given without expectation of praise, out of quiet duty, purifies the giver and loosens the knots of greed.

chapter: Chapter 8: The Power of Charity (Dana) and Selfless Giving
chapter_title: The Power of Charity (Dana) and Selfless Giving
text: Among all gifts, the gift of food to the hungry and the gift of fearlessness to the distressed are declared supreme. In nourishment resides life itself; he who sustains life sustains the divine.

chapter: Chapter 8: The Power of Charity (Dana) and Selfless Giving
chapter_title: The Power of Charity (Dana) and Selfless Giving
text: A gift offered with harsh words or disdain loses its virtue. True charity is accompanied by gentle eyes, respectful speech, and genuine joy in easing another's burden.

chapter: Chapter 10: The City of Justice and the Rule of Righteousness
chapter_title: The City of Justice and the Rule of Righteousness
text: The King of Justice judges not by worldly power or outward pretense, but by the intention of the heart and the righteousness of the life lived. Equity and mercy are the twin pillars of his court.

chapter: Chapter 10: The City of Justice and the Rule of Righteousness
chapter_title: The City of Justice and the Rule of Righteousness
text: Those who lived peacefully, who settled disputes with kindness and treated all creatures with goodwill, enter into joy and serenity. Their memory remains a light upon the earth.

chapter: Chapter 11: The Nature of Karma and Moral Agency
chapter_title: The Nature of Karma and Moral Agency
text: A person is his own best friend, and he is also his own worst enemy. When the mind is controlled and aligned with virtue, it acts as a steadfast guide; when uncontrolled, it drags the soul into confusion.

chapter: Chapter 11: The Nature of Karma and Moral Agency
chapter_title: The Nature of Karma and Moral Agency
text: None can escape the consequence of deeds done; yet by repentance, restitution, and turning wholeheartedly toward righteousness, the weight of past errors is softened and light enters the heart.

chapter: Chapter 11: The Nature of Karma and Moral Agency
chapter_title: The Nature of Karma and Moral Agency
text: As a calf finds its mother among a thousand cows, so does the past action find its doer. Therefore, let a wise person plant seeds of honesty and goodwill every single day.

chapter: Chapter 12: The Fruits of Virtuous Deeds and Truthfulness
chapter_title: The Fruits of Virtuous Deeds and Truthfulness
text: Truth is the highest dharma; upon truth the earth is established. A thousand sacrifices do not equal the merit of a life lived in unwavering truthfulness and simplicity.

chapter: Chapter 12: The Fruits of Virtuous Deeds and Truthfulness
chapter_title: The Fruits of Virtuous Deeds and Truthfulness
text: Patience (Kshama) is an ornament for the strong and a refuge for the weak. He who forgives offenses and bears difficulties without rancor attains tranquility that circumstance cannot disturb.

chapter: Chapter 12: The Fruits of Virtuous Deeds and Truthfulness
chapter_title: The Fruits of Virtuous Deeds and Truthfulness
text: Service rendered to aged parents and devoted teachers is equal to the worship of all sacred places. Their blessings bring longevity, discernment, and inward prosperity.

chapter: Chapter 13: Benevolence and Community Service
chapter_title: Benevolence and Community Service
text: Planting shade-giving trees along roads, digging wells for public use, and providing medicine to the sick—these acts yield enduring blessing both here and beyond. The welfare of the community is the welfare of the self.

chapter: Chapter 13: Benevolence and Community Service
chapter_title: Benevolence and Community Service
text: He who comforts a person in grief, who speaks encouraging words to the disheartened, performs a sacrifice more pleasing than rituals of gold and silver.

chapter: Chapter 14: Overcoming Anger and Cultivating Discernment
chapter_title: Overcoming Anger and Cultivating Discernment
text: From anger arises delusion, from delusion loss of memory, and from loss of memory destruction of discernment. When discernment is lost, a person falls from his noble estate. Guard the gates of speech against wrath.

chapter: Chapter 14: Overcoming Anger and Cultivating Discernment
chapter_title: Overcoming Anger and Cultivating Discernment
text: Envy is like a fire that consumes the vessel in which it is kept. To celebrate another's good fortune as one's own is the mark of a noble and liberated heart.

chapter: Chapter 15: The Yoga of Meditation and Equanimity
chapter_title: The Yoga of Meditation and Equanimity
text: Regard pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat with equal composure. He who is not elated in prosperity nor crushed in adversity has found the anchor of steady wisdom.

chapter: Chapter 15: The Yoga of Meditation and Equanimity
chapter_title: The Yoga of Meditation and Equanimity
text: The soul is neither born nor does it perish with the body. Knowing this eternal nature of life, one should act without fear, fulfilling duty with devotion and without anxiety for the outcome.

chapter: Chapter 16: Liberation and the Supreme Good
chapter_title: Liberation and the Supreme Good
text: Liberation is not attained by mere outward dress or scholastic disputation, but by knowing truth, practicing compassion, and realizing the oneness of life in all beings.

chapter: Chapter 16: Liberation and the Supreme Good
chapter_title: Liberation and the Supreme Good
text: He who sees all beings in himself and himself in all beings never despises anyone. In that vision of unity, all grief, fear, and sorrow vanish like mist before the morning sun.
